title: Salicylate Toxicity — Level & Management
sources: Done AK. Pediatrics 1960 (nomogram — now discredited); EXTRIP 2015 salicylate recommendations; AACT/ACMT guidance

changelog.change: Initial entry — from ED_ICU_OR_Calculators.xlsx. The Done nomogram is NOT used; management is level + clinical + acid-base + serial trend.

purpose: Frames an acute salicylate level against management thresholds. NOTE: the Done nomogram is unreliable (invalid with chronic use, enteric-coated or sustained-release product, ongoing absorption, acidaemia, or renal failure) and is NOT recommended — decisions rest on the clinical picture, acid–base status, and SERIAL levels every 2 h until clearly falling.

inputs.label: Hours since ingestion (context only — do not use to 'rule out')

interpretation.label: < 30 mg/dL — therapeutic to mildly elevated (therapeutic 10–20). If symptomatic or the history suggests a large or enteric-coated ingestion, repeat the level in 2 h before excluding toxicity; a single early level can rise substantially

30–50 mg/dL — mild toxicity (tinnitus, nausea, tachypnoea, primary respiratory alkalosis with a metabolic acidosis). Start IV fluids for volume/losses, give glucose-containing fluid (neuroglycopenia occurs with normal serum glucose), begin serum + urine alkalinisation (sodium bicarbonate infusion, target urine pH 7.5–8), replace potassium (alkalinisation fails if hypokalaemic), repeat level q2h

50–80 mg/dL — moderate to severe toxicity. Aggressive alkalinisation and K repletion; treat hyperthermia; get a blood gas and lactate. Consult toxicology and nephrology early. Haemodialysis if: altered mental status, cerebral or pulmonary oedema, renal failure, level rising despite alkalinisation, or pH ≤ 7.20

≥ 80 mg/dL (acute) — HAEMODIALYSIS indicated regardless of symptoms (EXTRIP: ≥ 90 mg/dL, or ≥ 80 with impaired kidney function). Also dialyse for any altered mental status, ARDS/pulmonary oedema needing oxygen, or a pH ≤ 7.20. Continue alkalinisation and never allow the pH to fall — if intubation is unavoidable, match the pre-intubation minute ventilation and give bicarbonate, or sudden death can follow

notes: CHRONIC toxicity (elderly, therapeutic-intent overuse) is more dangerous at any given level — significant toxicity and a dialysis indication can occur at 40–60 mg/dL. Do NOT be reassured by a 'normal-range' single level with a suggestive story (metabolic acidosis + respiratory alkalosis, anion gap, tinnitus). Avoid intubation if at all possible; if required, pre-oxygenate, use bicarbonate, and set a high minute ventilation to preserve respiratory compensation. Activated charcoal if within ~1–2 h or an enteric-coated/large ingestion; consider multi-dose charcoal for a rising level.
buildNote: Formula engine — level echoed with a mg/L conversion; Done nomogram deliberately not implemented. Bands reflect EXTRIP 2015 + standard management thresholds for ACUTE ingestion.
